messages.author: d80ddcad37e764f7
messages.subject: Plotting world map
parts:
When I use the standard world map contained in the 'maps' package it is very out of date (eg USSR rather than Russia etc)

So I tried using the data available on http://thematicmapping.org/downloads/world_borders.php - unzipping the download to C:\
library(rgdal)
world <- readOGR(dsn="C:/",layer="TM_WORLD_BORDERS-0.3")
plot(world)

This works and the map looks up-to-date, so then I try to move into ggplot2:
library(ggplot2)
world2 <- fortify(world)
and I get the error message 'Error in unionSpatialPolygons(cp, invert(polys)) : input lengths differ'

Has anyone encountered this problem / is there a simple way of doing the equivalent of world_df<-map_data("world") so it can be easily plotted in ggplot2?

Thanks

Peter Mennie

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Plotting world map
parts:
> When I use the standard world map contained in the 'maps' package it is very out of date (eg USSR rather than Russia etc)
>
> So I tried using the data available on http://thematicmapping.org/downloads/world_borders.php - unzipping the download to C:\
> library(rgdal)
> world <- readOGR(dsn="C:/",layer="TM_WORLD_BORDERS-0.3")
> plot(world)
>
> This works and the map looks up-to-date, so then I try to move into ggplot2:
> library(ggplot2)
> world2 <- fortify(world)
> and I get the error message 'Error in unionSpatialPolygons(cp, invert(polys)) : input lengths differ'

There's a simple fix for this:

world2 <- fortify(world, region = "ISO2")

The problem is that by default fortify uses the first column from
as.data.frame(world), which in this case happens to be FIPS. There
are three countries with missing fips codes: Palestine, Åland Islands
and United States Minor Outlying Islands. Due to a bug in fortify.df
(now fixed), these were getting dropped, giving the warning you
encountered. By telling fortify to split up the data by ISO2 code,
you avoid this problem and get what you actually want - separate
polygons for Palestine, Åland Islands and United States Minor Outlying
Islands.

Hadley
